comparison: Perfect agreement on infection susceptibility claims (C3, C47, C73-C79). Both evaluations find the survival curves, clinical scores, CFU measurements, and cell counts convincing with robust phenotypes and well-supported conclusions.

Perfect agreement on myeloid compartment defects (C6, C50-C51, C89-C97, C125). Both evaluations support the substantial impact of undernutrition on myelopoiesis with comprehensive flow cytometry data advancing understanding of malnutrition's hematopoietic effects.

Strong agreement on refeeding recovery of lymphoid parameters (C7-C8, C52, C100-C106, C128-C129). Both find recovery data well-supported with robust phenotypes, though peer review notes mechanistic understanding remains incomplete.

Strong agreement on persistent infection susceptibility after refeeding (C10-C11, C53, C56, C107-C110, C130). Both evaluations recognize this as an interesting and well-supported novel finding demonstrating dissociation between anatomical recovery and functional immunity.

Strong agreement on malnutrition model validation (C44, C61-C70). Both evaluations find the model nicely executed with robust phenotypes, consistent weight loss patterns, and organ-specific atrophy matching clinical definitions. OpenEval additionally references C58-C60, C65 not explicitly mentioned in peer review.

Strong agreement on differential recovery showing persistent myeloid defects (C12-C13, C54, C57, C116-C117, C121-C122, C143-C144). Both recognize this uncoupling of lymphoid vs. myeloid recovery as a central, well-supported finding. OpenEval includes additional claims C112-C115, C123 not explicitly addressed in peer review.

Strong agreement on T cell dysfunction (C4-C5, C49, C85-C88, C135-C138, C140). Both find conclusions well-supported with robust phenotypes. OpenEval additionally evaluates C48, C81-C83 regarding relative frequencies, which peer review does not explicitly address.

Moderate agreement on nutritional scarring conclusions (C14-C15, C55, C131, C147, C160-C161). Both find conclusions interesting and generally supported, but peer review emphasizes lack of mechanistic understanding. OpenEval includes C126-C127 not mentioned in peer review, and both note limitations in mechanistic claims.

Strong agreement on study limitations (C150-C154, C156). Both evaluations acknowledge these as appropriate caveats. Peer review notes most aspects were deferred experimentally but textual changes avoid over-interpretation. OpenEval additionally includes C155 which peer review groups with mechanistic uncertainty.

Agreement on uncertainty of epigenetic mechanism (C148). Both evaluations recognize this as speculative without direct experimental support. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN while peer review explicitly notes lack of mechanistic understanding. Peer review also includes C155 in this mechanistic uncertainty category.
